segments.en: Otzar HaYirah — Treasury of Awe | Volume IV (נ–ת)

This single-entry chapter is a sharp warning: compassion itself — the most essential human attribute — can be hijacked by the Sitra Achara. The pattern is ancient: those who caused the Golden Calf did so in the name of the people's welfare. And the same pattern repeats throughout history when movements that claim to act out of care for the Jewish people lead them away from Torah.

The Hebrew verse chosen for the chapter's opening — rachmei resha'im achzari, "the mercies of the wicked are cruel" — captures this precisely: the cruelest acts are often wrapped in the language of compassion. The antidote is the true Tzadik — who knows the difference between genuine mercy rooted in holiness and the pseudo-mercy that serves the Sitra Achara.
